definition: A patch lies closer to A when water has visible blue-green or gray reflectance and surface texture, or land forms open rectangular agricultural parcels. It lies closer to B when water is nearly black in both composites, or land has extensive dark-green woodland turning strongly red in false color. Use brightness together with spatial structure.
cues: Water: visible blue-green/gray tones and ripples toward A; nearly black, featureless surfaces toward B.
Land: straight boundaries and rectangular fields toward A; irregular, continuous wooded areas toward B.
Vegetation: varied green, muted red or pink parcels toward A; extensive vivid-red canopy toward B.
